input.brief: concept preview for La Della Caterers and events in Puthencruz

direction.name: The sentence is the layout
direction.idea: The page is an argument in plain sentences, each with its evidence beside it. The first screen is one short sentence about the subject that a visitor can check against the picture next to it ('Every loaf leaves the oven by six', beside the racks at six): the sentence sets the grid and the measure, and the picture stands beside it or opens full width right after it, never inside it. Write the sentences first, from the inventory, one claim each; then give each the one thing that proves it: a photograph, a figure, a short list, the product doing it. The reader believes the page because every sentence is shown.
direction.composition: First screen: the sentence, four to seven words on two lines at the dealt display step, flush to the left margin across columns 1–7, with one supporting sentence and the action under it on the same edge. The picture it names fills columns 8–12 at the full height of the screen and ends on the right margin; or, when the sentence takes the full width, the picture runs across the width directly under it, cropped by the bottom of the screen (never on a software page: its interface stands beside the sentence). Later sections repeat the grammar at a smaller scale: a heading of one short sentence on the left half and its proof on the right half (a photograph, a figure with its unit, a short list, an interface fragment), top-aligned with it, so the page reads as a series of sentences with evidence. Every sentence starts on the same left edge, and no picture sits between words or between lines. The space between sections as section 0 deals it.
direction.typography: Display weight with real presence (medium to bold), tracking -0.03 to -0.05em, leading 0.95–1.0 so two lines sit close. The sentences are real sentences: sentence case, with a full stop on every one or on none.
direction.colour: A calm ground with ink at full contrast. The colour comes from the pictures beside the sentences; if the palette has an accent, use it once, on the action.
direction.imagery: One strong photograph of what the first sentence says, large enough to check it against the words: beside the sentence on the first screen, or full width right after it. Every later picture is the proof of the sentence next to it, at a size that shows what it is. Never a picture inside a sentence, between its words or in its letters: that is a generated-page tell, and the inspector fails it.
direction.richness: Sentences a reader can check, each paired with the thing that proves it. The first picture is read as the evidence for the headline, so choose it with care: it shows exactly what the sentence says, large.
direction.pitfalls: The sentence must be short enough for two lines on a phone (about 32 characters). Do not style one word differently to stress it. Do not put a picture inside the sentence to make it an idea: the idea is the match between what the sentence says and what the picture shows. A sentence with no proof beside it is a slogan; cut it or find its proof.

hero.name: Lone centred word with three-part foot row
hero.blueprint: A one-screen hero on the dealt ground, 100svh, the dealt navigation on top. A single bold word dead centre at the display step, one line (a word of the page's own idea, in the display face, leading 0.9), the only display element. Along the bottom, 80px up and inside the page margins, one three-part row on one baseline at the body step: left a place and a date, centre a two-line sentence (max 300px, 12 words, centred), right the dealt button. The word and the row arrive with the dealt entrance. Colour roles: the dealt ground and ink, accent = the button. House rules for it: No issue number, tiny caption, partner logo or icon row; the foot row is a place and a date, one sentence and one button. The word is a word of the page's idea, not the company name, and no hover effect colours it.
hero.mobile: The word at the display step on one line (two stacked if long); the foot row becomes two rows: the place and date, then the sentence, then the full-width dealt button.
hero.headline: The page's own idea, in this client's words, on two lines at most (12 words or fewer).
hero.signature: One bold word at the display step stands alone dead centre of an otherwise bare screen, with a three-part foot row on one baseline 80px above the bottom edge: place and date left, a two-line sentence centre, the dealt button right.

palette.name: Deep, rich olive
palette.note: Deep ground (#161d26), light ink, one rich olive accent. The accent is for the primary action, links and at most one other thing on a screen; it is never a ground for text blocks, never a second headline colour and never spread across cards. Two grounds, no field: the page ground and --surface, a clear step from it; sections are told apart by space, size and pictures. Every other colour on the page comes from photographs or the product, never from added tints, badges or chips.

type.name: Archivo Black over Petrona

text.settings: weight 400 for running text, 600 for emphasis and buttons, leading 1.5, 60-72 characters a line

type.note: A sans display over a serif text. A 1.5 scale from a 17px body; the hero's display step is about 5vw at 1440. Six steps and no others: small, body, lead, sub, head, display. Archivo Black only for the display and head steps; Petrona for everything a visitor reads at length, buttons and navigation included. Load only the weights listed; a weight the face lacks is faked by the browser and the inspector fails it.

motion.name: Rolling figures
motion.description: For a page whose case is a handful of numbers (a report, a fund, a practice with a founding year): three or four figures at display size roll each digit up to its value once as they come into view, about 1.1 seconds on a strong ease-out, the columns 70ms apart. Tabular figures, the real number kept in the text for screen readers and search, never in running text and never for a value that changes after load. Set at its value under reduced motion. Recipe: 'Rolling figures' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: Headline crossing onto a photograph
sections.blueprint: A white or pale ground. A photograph taller than it is wide, 720px wide (columns 7–12), ends on the right page margin with its top at 46% of the section's first screen and runs below the fold. The heading starts on the 32px left margin across columns 1–8: two lines of light-weight serif capitals at clamp(64px, 5.6vw, 88px), leading 1.04, the first line starting 34% down the screen and the second placed so that its right half runs onto the photograph's upper-left corner. Choose a picture whose upper-left quarter is pale enough for the ink, or set the second line twice, in the ink and in the paper colour, each copy clipped to its side of the photograph's left edge. Under the heading on columns 1–5, one paragraph of up to 25 words at 22px, leading 1.4. At the bottom-left a second, smaller photograph of 360×400px enters, cropped by the screen's lower edge, and on the next screen becomes the left half of a staggered pair with the large one. Nothing else is on the screen.
sections.mobile: The heading sits at 10vw on two lines on the 20px margin. The photograph becomes 75% of the content width, ending on the right margin, and starts under the heading's first line so the second line crosses its top-left corner. The paragraph follows at 17px, then the small photograph at 50% of the width on the left margin.

sections.name: One item per poster line
sections.blueprint: A short list set as a poster. Four to seven items (services, headline acts, courses, opening days) stack one per line at clamp(64px, 10vw, 150px) in the display weight, all capitals or all lowercase, leading 0.92, flush left at a 20px margin on a flat field. Its one detail (a price, a date, a time range) sits at the right margin on the same baseline at 18–20px with tabular figures, so the page has two alignments only: giant words left, small facts right. Items too long for one line at this size are shortened, not shrunk. Between items there is only the tight leading. Hovering an item swaps its ink for the accent. There is no heading: the first item starts 80px below the section top and the last ends 80px above the bottom. The list reuses the hero title's exact type size, so it reads as another poster.
sections.mobile: Items at 15vw, one per line, flush left with 16px margins. Each detail moves beneath its item at 15px, left-aligned, with 6px above and 22px below. If any single word is wider than the screen at 15vw, drop the whole list to 12vw rather than breaking a word.

sections.name: The itemised receipt
sections.blueprint: For offers made of parts: a base price plus options, a kit, a bundle. A tall paper-coloured slip 380px wide sits in columns 8–11 on a contrasting ground, its bottom edge cut into a zigzag with `clip-path: polygon()`, its top edge running off the top of the section. On the slip, with 28px padding: the name centred at 20px bold, then each item as a row with the description left and the amount right at 16px with tabular figures, 14px between rows; a thick 4px bar in the ink colour; then the total as the largest thing on the slip at 44px, right-aligned. Columns 1–6 carry the heading (two to four words at about 4vw), one paragraph at 18px and the button, starting 96px from the top. If options are selectable, ticking one in the left column adds its row to the slip and updates the total.
sections.mobile: Heading, paragraph and any options come first. The slip follows at 86% width, centred, keeping its zigzag foot, with rows at 16px and the total at 36px. The button sits under the slip at full width, 52px tall.

sections.name: Three photographs, then a field
sections.blueprint: Two parts with no gap between them. First, a strip of three photographs butted edge to edge across the full viewport, each one third wide and 40svh tall, `object-fit: cover`, no gutters and no captions; give all three the same treatment. Directly beneath, a band in one flat palette colour, about 44svh tall. In the band, columns 1–7: the closing statement at 26–30px over three lines in the band's assigned ink, with exactly one phrase underlined by a 4px bar (`text-decoration-thickness: 4px; text-underline-offset: 6px`), and that phrase is the link; two lines at 16px follow 32px lower. In the lower-right corner, columns 11–12, a small portrait photograph (4:5, about 150px wide) sits 40px from the band's edges: the person who will answer. There is no button; the underlined phrase is the action.
sections.mobile: The strip becomes one full-width photograph at 4:3 with the other two side by side beneath it at half width each, still gutterless. The band follows: statement at 22px, the two small lines, and the portrait at 96px wide in the bottom-right corner.

references.name: Rows
references.idea: Radical understatement: a product about simple lists is sold with a 27px headline, 12px copy and a column of small live demos, each proving one interaction.
references.hero: Warm off-white page, almost empty. Everything hangs on one vertical line 27% in from the left. A small striped-letter logo mark sits there near the top; 220px lower comes a two-line headline at only 27px (under 2vw), then three lines of 13px body about 370px wide, then a near-black rectangular button with 4px corners beside a text link with an arrow. A single grey sign-in link sits in the top-right corner; there is no navigation bar. More than 80% of the viewport is blank. At the bottom edge the first feature module peeks in: grey demo panel left, short text column right.
references.type: Suisse Intl only, weight 450–500, tracking −0.04em. Headline 27px, feature headings about 16px on two lines, body 12px. Three sizes in total, no uppercase and no display moment; hierarchy comes from weight and empty space alone.
references.colour: #f5f6f1 #e6e7e1 #1a191d #ffffff #c7372f #3aa56a — Warm paper off-white with slightly darker grey-green demo panels and near-black type; colour appears only inside the UI as priority dots, outlined status pills and one green or red action button.
references.imagery: No pictures: small live-rendered fragments of the app (two or three white list rows with dots, status pills, avatars and a visible cursor) sit in flat grey panels of fixed 368px width with barely rounded corners.
references.layout: One content block about 650px wide, offset left of centre, repeated down the page: 368px demo panel plus a 245px text column, top-aligned, separated by 200px or more of empty space. The logo mark sticks to the top-left corner on scroll. Footer is one line.

sections.description: The repeating module: a flat grey panel roughly 368px wide and 120–190px tall holding a tiny mock list (white rows with 6px radius, a coloured numbered dot at left, task title, an outlined status pill, an avatar, a chevron) and often a cursor mid-action. To its right, 20px away and top-aligned, a medium-weight heading of one or two lines and two short paragraphs at 11–12px in a column only 245px wide. Modules never alternate sides; they stack with large gaps.

The closing block keeps the same narrow measure: a three-line paragraph at 13px, then the identical button and arrow-link pair from the hero, left-aligned on the text column's axis. After a long gap a single hairline spans the 650px block and under it sits one row of tiny footer text: brand line at left, six links and a copyright strung along the right.

steal: Set the headline at near-body size (under 2vw) and let empty space, not scale, give it importance.
Explain each feature with a tiny cropped fragment of real UI in a fixed-width flat panel, one interaction per panel, with the cursor left visible.
Hang the whole page on one off-centre left edge and never break it, logo and footer included.

references.name: Noho
references.idea: Furniture sold through people misusing it (wearing, balancing on, hiding behind chairs on flat colour backdrops) while the interface stays quiet beige.
references.hero: The viewport splits exactly 50/50 by tone alone: left half warm off-white, right half a slightly darker greige, no rule. Left: a small lowercase logo top-left at 30px margin, then a four-line bold headline at 60px (4.2vw), tracking -0.04em and leading near 1.0, top-left aligned and filling the upper 40%; the lower half is empty except for a one-line 18px tagline pinned bottom-left. Right: a staggered mosaic of seven portrait photos, each about 175 by 230px with 15px gaps, on a four-column, three-row grid with several cells left empty and the rightmost image cropped by the viewport edge. A white square menu button sits top-right.
references.type: Switzer only. Headlines weight 600, tracking -0.04em, sentence case, charcoal rather than black; statements at 60px, body 13.5px, meta labels about 11px grey. The digest records one element at 15.6vw. Roughly four sizes, one family, no caps.
references.colour: #f1eee9 #e7e2dc #cdc0b0 #3c3c3c #b4a5db #f2e05a — The interface is three close warm beiges with charcoal type; saturated colour (lilac, yellow, olive, terracotta, sand) exists only in photo backdrops and the products themselves.
references.imagery: Studio shots of people interacting oddly with chairs on seamless single-colour backdrops, portrait 3:4, square corners; plus very large cut-out product shots on beige with a soft radial glow and contact shadow, cropped by the panel edge.
references.layout: Outer margins of 16-30px. Sections alternate between split halves, centred statements and left-aligned headings over card rows. Cards are flat rectangles one tone darker than the page with 8px gaps, content pinned to the top-left and bottom edges. Wide empty bands separate sections.

sections.description: A centred four-line statement at about 60px bold with tiny square photo thumbnails, roughly one cap-height tall, dropped inline between words like emoji. Directly beneath, the page splits into two full-width flat colour halves (light greige and tan), each with a small circled plus button in its top inner corner; these are the tops of the two product panels.

Two side-by-side panels in different beiges, each dominated by one enormous cut-out chair (one yellow, one black) cropped at the top so mostly seat and legs show, with a soft radial highlight behind. Along the bottom of each panel: a tiny label and price at left, a row of colour-swatch dots, then two small rectangular buttons at right, one white and one charcoal.

Three equal flat tiles in a row with 8px gaps, each about 210px tall. One short claim is centred in each at roughly 18px, and an index number sits alone in the bottom-left corner in 11px. A small bulleted label hangs above each tile. After a large empty gap, another centred bold statement begins.

A horizontal strip of colour-backdrop photos bleeds off both edges at the top of the section. Below, a left-aligned bold heading at about 40px, then a row of beige cards overflowing to the right: each has an @name at top-left, a short paragraph in 11px, and a bottom row with star glyphs left and a small text link right.

steal: Split the hero 50/50 by background tone alone, park the headline top-left and one tagline bottom-left, and fill the other half with a staggered photo mosaic that leaves grid cells empty.
Keep the interface in three close beige tones and confine all saturated colour to photo backdrops and products, so the photography becomes the palette.
Drop cap-height photo thumbnails inline between the words of a large centred statement.
references.media: A stepped mosaic of seven 175x231 studio photographs (people doing odd things with a chair against one saturated backdrop each) covers about 22% of the fold on the darker right half, bleeding off the right edge; the left half is type. Below come photo chips between the words of a statement, two product halves each with a live 3D chair on its own tone, an auto-scrolling row of portrait tiles, a pinned card deck, and a sticky 3D chair card beside an accordion; square corners everywhere, no video.
references.motion: About 1s of entrance with no preloader: headline lines rise through masks while the mosaic tiles arrive one by one. Lenis holds sticky product halves and pins a story deck for +=400% (3600px), each step bringing the next card in from the right and compressing earlier ones into slivers, and the footer is uncovered by a scrubbed mask over a 728px runway as its slogan letters rise over 1.04s at a 0.04s stagger; micro-interactions are GSAP nudges of 0.2-0.4s on custom eases, and the 3D chairs turn on drag.

references.name: Rendez-vous Francéclat
references.idea: A hot gradient sliced into three glass panes that double as the column grid for navigation and content.
references.hero: A full-viewport gradient runs from white at the far left through orange to crimson on the right, sliced into three equal vertical panes that each restart the gradient, like fluted glass. There is no nav bar: mono uppercase links sit as plain stacks (3, 3, 2) at the top-left of each pane, 24px in; an outlined language select top-right. At 37–63% height on the left: a stacked light-caps programme logo, then the event name in heavy lowercase grotesk on two lines, about 7vw, with two mono metadata blocks above aligned to column starts and a sponsor logo below. The right half is empty colour. A black rectangular CTA sits bottom-right.
references.type: ABC Diatype throughout: heavy, tightly tracked lowercase for the event name and 68px section heads (-0.03em), medium 22–28px for statements and paragraphs. A monospaced cut in uppercase 14px handles nav, dates and numbered labels. A stacked light-caps logo adds a third voice.
references.colour: #f8652b #de194b #ffffff #000000 #fcd9c8 #6f7478 — Orange-to-crimson gradient for hero and footer, fading out to pure white for the informational middle; one desaturated grey photo section. Text black on gradient and white, pale peach in the footer. Warm throughout.
references.imagery: The paned gradient is the main image. One full-bleed grey architectural photo with a blurred figure; a pale isometric line drawing of the venue; logos. No product photography visible.
references.layout: Built on thirds and a visible column grid: nav stacks, metadata and text blocks all start on column lines, and white sections expose the vertical hairlines. Left-anchored; large empty areas on the right. Gradient, photo and white sections alternate over 20 screens.

sections.description: As the hero scrolls, the gradient pales to white at the bottom and a two-line bold 28px statement sits in the right third, aligned to the third pane's edge. Next, a full-bleed grey architectural photo carries two paragraphs of white 22px text across the full width with 16px margins, the second at reduced opacity. The event lockup reappears ghosted at the bottom with mono practical details and a white rectangular CTA.

White field with the column grid exposed as vertical hairlines. A bold 40px heading resolves from blur at lower-left. Then a pale isometric line drawing of the venue spans the left four columns, a narrow paragraph about 230px wide sits mid-page, and along the bottom numbered items step down column by column: mono index above an underlined mono uppercase link.

Footer. The paned gradient returns. A partner name top-left; a two-line bold 36px sign-off in pale peach; a newsletter heading with a white input joined to a black button and a consent checkbox. The right two panes hold small bold link lists under mono labels. A hairline and a mono legal row close it.

steal: Slice a full-bleed gradient into three vertical panes that each restart the gradient to get a fluted-glass look from colour alone.
Distribute the navigation as plain mono text stacks at the top of each pane instead of a nav bar, so the grid is the header.
Leave the layout grid's vertical hairlines visible in white sections and step numbered items down along the columns.

scenes.name: A hand dealt one card per beat
scenes.principle: Cards are dealt one at a time onto a pile, each arriving turned (tilted in the plane, or swung in from edge-on) and settling at its own small angle on top of the last, either fanned along a huge arc or levelled almost flat, while a title holds beside or beneath them, so a short set of items is laid down like a hand of cards being played.
scenes.freshTake: For a type foundry's four weights: tall paper strips hang from the top edge of the screen like pendants on an arc whose centre sits far above the viewport, and each beat swings a new strip in from the left in a hard 150 ms snap with no spring, the set re-centring as it lands. Strips alternate ground and ink, told apart by colour alone with no edge line or shadow, and each carries its weight's name set in that weight, large enough to read on the covered strips. Four strips at about half a screen each, and the section releases on the full set.
scenes.breaksWhen: The fan needs about 940 px of width for four cards; phones need a vertical fan or a plain stack. More than five cards spread past a laptop screen. Stepping relative to the last step leaves cards missing after a reload mid-pin or a hard fling; set every card from the current step. Body text on covered cards is unreadable, so only the top card is really read. A colour per card breaks the house palette, overlapping cards alternate ground and ink rather than take an edge line or a shadow, and big 1-2-3-4 numerals on the cards are banned numbering.

scenes.name: Page lifts off a closing picture
scenes.summary: The last content section slides up like a sheet, at its full width and in its own ground, and uncovers a picture that was held underneath it all along; while the sheet clears the screen the picture settles from a close 1.35x zoom to its natural framing, landing exactly as the scroll runs out. A solid band across the top third carries the closing line, a headline at display size, and the contact block in the body face, in the picture's own top-edge colour, so band and picture meet with no seam, and the whole picture is the page's one action with a plain label at its foot. The picture is a photograph, or a full-bleed close crop of the product's interface built in HTML (data-ui) whose app bar takes the band's colour, so a page can close on its product rather than a photograph.
scenes.place: The end of the page: the contact or the call to action, straight after the last content section, which becomes the sheet that lifts (give it a screen of height or more). The footer after it is a designed section of its own and follows the finished frame: leave `foot` unset (it pulls the element it names over the stage's foot, so it suits only a page that ends on the scene). Once per page, and never right after another scene: the section that lifts is the quiet section between them.
scenes.content: One picture and one line. Photo mode: one photograph 2400px wide or more (3000+ for full sharpness at the 1.35x start), its top edge even (fog, sky, a plain wall, a table top) and its subject in the lower half; a busy or textured top edge shows the seam, so smooth it or redraw. Interface mode: a close crop of the real product in HTML with data-ui, full bleed with no card, frame or rounded edge: an app bar in var(--lift-band-c) (so it meets the band with no seam), a title and two to four rows at true size (labels 14px or more at 1440, any heading in it under 24px), believable figures that add up, one item picked; side padding var(--lift-ui-inset). Its words end in the top ~37% of the stage (about 335px at 1440x900) because it grows 1.35x from its top edge and must never pass under the label; the rest is the product's own empty surface, where the label sits. Its CSS under [data-ui]. Words: a closing line of 3-7 words (h2, display face at clamp(40px, 5vw, 80px) over seven columns, two lines at most), a contact block of one to three short paragraphs at body size (address, email and phone, hours; never a giant name or email), and a label of 1-3 words for the one action. --lift-band set to the photograph's top-edge sample at 1440x900 for no script (the script samples it live), or to a tone step of --ground in interface mode.
scenes.options: mode 'photo' | 'ui' (default from data-ui on .lift-media); settle 1.35 (1.1-1.5) the start scale, 1 at the end of the scroll; phoneSettle 1.18 (1.05-1.3); lift 1 (0.9-1) the sheet's scale as it leaves (under 1 pulls its sides in over the picture: old pages only); dim 0 (0-0.3) how much it darkens (over 0 turns the page's ground into a grey slab: old pages only); band 'auto' (the median of the photograph's top edge as cropped on this screen; same-origin pictures, or CORS ones with crossorigin="anonymous") | 'token' (--lift-band; the default in ui mode) | a CSS colour, and a dark band turns its words to --ground; focus the settle's transform-origin ('50% 0%', so the seam row never changes, in both modes); label 'foot' | 'centre'; sheet a selector for the section that lifts (default the element before the scene); foot unset by default (the designed footer follows the scene); a selector pulls that element over the picture's foot so the scroll ends on the settled frame, only for a page that ends on the scene with one plain line; scrub true (locked) or 0.1-1 s; phone 'same' | 'rest'. The hold is not an option: it is the lift, the sheet's height up to one screen. Each word block lands whole on a short clock once the sheet's edge has cleared it.
scenes.phone: The same lift: the picture stays held under the page while it slides away at its full width, with a gentler 1.18x settle. The band grows with its words (a 32-40px title over a two-column contact block, about 32-37% of the screen, the words low in it so the title lands by about 0.9 of the lift) instead of squeezing them, the label sits just above the footer line, and the interface crop stays full bleed but drops to the columns that fit, its words inset by --lift-ui-inset so none leaves the screen at the start scale. phone: 'rest' gives the finished composition.

nav.text: No bar: the wordmark at the top-left margin (h3 step) and four one-word links at the top right with the one action as the dealt button at the right margin. After 80px of scroll the wordmark swaps for a 48px monogram tile (ink fill, ground letter) by a crossfade with a 6px upward slide (240ms), and the four links collapse into one Menu button 48px tall in the surface tone beside the action. The action stays visible throughout. Menu opens the links in a full-screen sheet on the ink (the surface tone on a dark page). Everything that stays fixed stands on a solid fill. Hover: the Menu button's fill swaps to the ink. On a phone: the monogram tile at the left, the Menu button and the action at the right from the start, at the page margin. House rules for it: The mascot mark is replaced by a typeset monogram; the fixed tile and Menu button are solid; the action stays outside the trigger so it remains in reach.
nav.signature: At the top the wordmark and four links; after 80px of scroll the wordmark swaps for a 48px monogram tile and the four links fold into one Menu button beside the always-visible action.
nav.name: Corner wordmark becomes a monogram, links fold into a Menu button

footer.text: A newsletter block on the page ground: one filled card on the surface tone with the dealt corner, whatever the page's card style, across eight columns, holding one sentence at the h3 step and an email field with its button in one row; beside it, on four columns, the contact and two or three links; the legal line and Image credits under both. It is the page's one email form.
footer.signature: One filled card across eight columns with a sentence at the h3 step and the email field and its button in one row.

cards.text: Rows with a surface: each item a full-width row on the surface tone, 80-104px tall, 8px apart, the dealt corner: the name at the h4 step on the left, one fact in the middle columns, the price or the link at the right. No line between them, no outline; hover steps the fill. For a menu, the plans, the rooms in short, a schedule. On a phone each row sets its parts on two lines.
cards.signature: Full-width filled rows 80-104px tall, 8px apart: the name at the left, one fact in the middle, the price or link at the right.

buttons.text: A label with a round arrow: the label at 18-20px in the ink, weight 500, then 12px on a 52-56px circle filled with the accent holding an arrow in the accent's ink; label and circle are one link, 56px tall; hover turns the arrow 45° and slides the label 4px. The second action is the label alone, without the circle.
buttons.signature: A label followed by a 52-56px circle in the accent holding an arrow that turns 45 degrees on hover; label and circle are one link.

corners.text: A 4px radius on cards, panels and fields; pictures square or at the same 4px.

spacing.text: Standard: 16-20vh between sections (about 144-180px at 1440 by 900, 96-120px on a phone), page margins 32-48px at 1440 and 20px on a phone.

treatment.text: One grade over every picture (slightly warm or slightly cool, a little lifted shadows), the same on all of them.

interaction.text: No interactive widget. The page is read: its content, pictures and motion carry it. Controls are the navigation, the links, the action and any real form.

clip.text: One moving picture of the subject: a muted loop with a poster frame and a pause control, used once, large. Only if an honest clip of this subject exists.

entrance.name: Exposure
entrance.summary: the photograph's light and colour come up from pale
entrance.sees: The type is in place at once. The photograph starts pale, as if over-exposed (dim on a dark page), and its real light and colour come up in about a second.
entrance.markup: Use it on a mid-tone or dark photograph: on a pale one the change barely shows and reads as a glitch. A photo treatment's filter goes on the frame, never on the img or video.

byImagery.photo: A photograph or a clip. base.css animates the img's or video's own filter, so a caption in the frame stays at full ink.

below.label: Pictures take their colour
below.rule: Large pictures (data-reveal="picture", four at most) go from 20% saturation to full colour once as they enter, over 900 ms with ease. No travel, no scale, and text never moves.

moves.name: Brackets close in
moves.description: A single word or two short words set large as the section's statement (display step, display face, ink, centred), flanked by two bracket glyphs from the same face at 1.2x the word's height. Scrubbed by scroll (from 85% to 50% of the viewport height) the brackets start 300px further out on each side and slide inward until they sit 0.2em from the word; the word itself is always fully visible. After landing everything holds still; a paragraph (lead step, 44 characters) sits 56px under it. Ground as dealt, accent none. Phone: word at the head step, brackets travel 120px. House rules for it: Never a small bracketed label above a heading (an eyebrow): the brackets are typographic marks around the large statement word itself; the page's own face, never a monospace; brackets stay ink, not a styled accent; scroll-linked, so the dealt entrance stands.

moves.name: Alternate side slide
moves.description: Three or four rows, each full width inside the page margins (about 1296px at 1440): one big photograph tile (560x560, the dealt corner) and a caption block (a title at the head step and one paragraph of about 20 words at 20px, 44 characters wide) filling the other half, so no row is empty at the left. Odd rows put the tile on the left, even rows on the right. As a row crosses from 90% to 50% of the viewport height the tile slides 180px into its place from its outer side and the caption 180px into its place from the opposite side, scrubbed, both fully visible throughout; at rest both are in place. Every row sits on the same ground, with no second fill. The dealt section space between rows. Phone: tile above caption, each moves 40px from alternating sides. House rules for it: The tile is a photograph, never a digit or a headline in a card (no 01/02/03 numbering); no outlined tiles; no row left empty on one side; scroll-linked, nothing starts hidden.
